# Running the ionium fuzzer locally

The fuzzer (<https://github.com/ionium-ap/Archipelago-fuzzer>) generates multiworlds against
a source checkout of Archipelago and reports failures. It runs entirely offline against your
working tree -- no release or published URL needed, so this should run before every tag.

In short:

    scripts/run_fuzzer.ps1 -Setup             # once, and again to refresh the fuzzer
    scripts/fuzzer_prepare.ps1                # build, and enter the prepared state
    scripts/run_fuzzer.ps1                    # the failure rate the index measures
    scripts/run_fuzzer.ps1 -Pass checks       # each counted hook, one pass each
    scripts/run_fuzzer.ps1 -Pass canary       # proves the pipeline still reports failures
    scripts/run_index_tests.ps1               # the full core suite against the build
    scripts/fuzzer_cleanup.ps1                # back to the development state

Read "Why passes" below before changing how the fuzzer is invoked.

## Prerequisite: a configured clone

The fuzzer runs Archipelago from source, so it needs everything `scripts/setup.ps1` creates:

- `Archipelago/`, the clone of Archipelago the fuzzer runs in, with the world link at
  `Archipelago/worlds/khimera_damg` that the build goes through;
- `.py-env/venv`, the venv with Archipelago's requirements installed, which the fuzzer runs on;
- `.py-env/python`, the interpreter that venv was made from.

The Python bundled with the installed Archipelago at `C:\ProgramData\Archipelago` cannot stand
in for these: it is a frozen cx_Freeze app with no `python.exe`, `pip` or `venv` of its own.

## Where things live

- `fuzzer/` holds the upstream fuzzer (`fuzz.py`, `hooks/`, its `README.md` and `LICENSE`, and a
  `COMMIT` file naming the commit it was cloned at), plus three things of this repository's own:
  `khimera_damg.yaml` (the fuzz-meta file), the `empty-apworld/` clone, and `runs/` (the run
  archives). Its `.gitignore`, generated by `-Setup`, is `*` followed by `!khimera_damg.yaml`, so
  the fuzz-meta file is the only thing in the folder git tracks.
- `Archipelago/` is where `fuzz.py` actually runs. `fuzz.py` puts its own folder on `sys.path` to
  import Archipelago, so it and `hooks/` are copied into the Archipelago root (by `-Setup` and by
  `scripts/fuzzer_prepare.ps1`). `custom_worlds/empty.apworld`, `static_worlds/empty.yaml`,
  `fuzz.py`'s own `fuzz_output/` and, while prepared, the built `.apworld` and
  `kdamg_prepared.json` land there too. `Archipelago/` is disposable, and
  `scripts/restore_archipelago.ps1` deletes all of it; the next prepare puts back what it needs.

## One-time setup

    scripts/run_fuzzer.ps1 -Setup

This:

1. checks that `Archipelago/` and `.py-env/venv` exist, and stops with a pointer to
   `scripts/setup.ps1` if not;
2. clones the fuzzer into `fuzzer/upstream-staging` and strips its `.git`. A nested `.git` would
   make the outer repository treat `fuzzer/` as an opaque boundary, and `khimera_damg.yaml` could
   then not be committed. The commit it was cloned at goes into `fuzzer/COMMIT`;
3. only once the clone succeeded, deletes the previous upstream files from `fuzzer/` and moves the
   new ones in. `khimera_damg.yaml`, `empty-apworld/` and `runs/` are left alone. If upstream ever
   ships something under one of those names, the setup stops before deleting anything;
4. writes `fuzzer/.gitignore`;
5. copies `fuzz.py` and `hooks/` into `Archipelago/`, replacing the old `hooks/` folder rather than
   copying over it, so a hook removed upstream does not linger;
6. runs `scripts/fuzzer/build_empty_apworld.ps1 -Force`, described under "The Empty world".

Every step stops the setup on failure and says why. If an old upstream file cannot be deleted --
usually because a terminal is standing inside `fuzzer/` -- the new clone is left in
`fuzzer/upstream-staging`.

Re-run `-Setup` to pick up a newer fuzzer or empty-apworld. The fuzzer has no requirements of its
own beyond Archipelago's, so there is no separate venv to maintain: it runs on `.py-env/venv`.

## Prepare, run, clean up

The fuzzer tests the built `.apworld`, which cannot be loaded while the world link is in
`worlds/`: Archipelago loads world folders before `.apworld` files, and skips an `.apworld` whose
game is already loaded, with only a warning. So fuzzing happens in the *prepared* state, and
everything else (building, `scripts/run_tests.ps1`) in the *development* state. "Build states" in
`CLAUDE.md` describes both; `scripts/build/build_state.ps1` defines them.

    scripts/fuzzer_prepare.ps1

1. builds `khimera_damg.apworld` through `scripts/build_apworld.ps1`, which needs the link, and
   checks that it produced a new `Archipelago/build/apworlds/khimera_damg.apworld`;
2. copies `fuzz.py` and `hooks/` into `Archipelago/`, and builds `custom_worlds/empty.apworld`
   from the existing clone if it is missing;
3. removes the world link and installs the build in `Archipelago/custom_worlds/`;
4. writes `Archipelago/kdamg_prepared.json`, recording the build's SHA-256 and a fingerprint of
   `khimera_damg/` (every file except `tests/` and `__pycache__/`).

Run on an already prepared `Archipelago/`, it cleans up first and prepares again with a fresh
build: do that after every change to `khimera_damg/`.

    scripts/run_fuzzer.ps1 [-Pass <pass>[,<pass>...]] [-Runs 500] [-Jobs 16] [-Yamls 1] [-Timeout 15]

Each run checks that `Archipelago/` is prepared and that the installed build is still the one the
prepare recorded and still matches `khimera_damg/`, and stops otherwise. It then runs each
requested pass through `scripts/fuzzer/run_fuzz_pass.ps1`, which repeats that check, prints a
summary table, and exits non-zero unless every pass came back `ok`. It never builds and never
touches the world link, so a run that is stopped or killed leaves the state as it was.

    scripts/run_index_tests.ps1

runs Archipelago's full core suite against the installed build, the way the index does; see
"Hard requirements for inclusion" in `CLAUDE.md`.

    scripts/fuzzer_cleanup.ps1

removes the build, the state file and any canary world a killed canary pass left behind, and
recreates the world link. `fuzz.py`, `hooks/` and `empty.apworld` stay for the next prepare.

While prepared, `build_apworld.ps1`, `run_tests.ps1` and `setup_world_link.ps1` refuse to run and
say to clean up first. If a script finds `Archipelago/` in neither state -- say, a prepare killed
between removing the link and writing the state file -- it lists what is wrong and points at
`scripts/restore_archipelago.ps1`, which always ends in the development state.

The build goes through `scripts/build_apworld.ps1` rather than zipping the folder directly,
because a hand-made zip carries the source `archipelago.json`, which deliberately omits `version`
and `compatible_version`; without those, Archipelago cannot read the manifest and loads the world
with no version metadata at all.

It also has to be a real `.apworld` zip in `custom_worlds/`, not a directory link there:
Archipelago imports every world as `worlds.<name>`, and only `Archipelago/worlds/` and the
`.apworld` meta-path finder can satisfy that import. A folder in `custom_worlds/` is found while
indexing but fails to import.

### Passes

| Pass | Hooks loaded | Empty | `--skip-output` | Fails when |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rate` (default) | none | yes | no | the failure rate is 1% or more |
| `gerpocalypse` | `gerpocalypse` | no (the hook adds Kingdom Hearts) | yes | any failure |
| `indirect_conditions` | that hook | yes | yes | any failure |
| `item_location_count` | that hook | yes | yes | any failure |
| `detect_rule_variable_capture_issues` | that hook | yes | yes | any failure |
| `check_placement_item_location_references` | that hook | yes | yes | any failure |
| `detect_output_placement_changes` | that hook | yes | **no** | any failure |
| `determinism` | `determinism` | yes | yes | any failure; runs at half the jobs and twice the timeout |

`checks` expands to the six counted passes and `all` to `rate` followed by them. `determinism` and
`canary` are never part of either; ask for them by name.

The `rate` pass is the index's measurement: failures plus timeouts, divided by generations that
did not end in an `OptionError`. It adds `--dump-ignored`, because this world rolls no invalid
option combinations, so an ignored generation is worth a look; the summary flags any.

A check pass has no rate. Its hook reclassifies everything it is not testing, so its counts say
only whether that one hook found anything.

`-Yamls` takes a number or a range such as `1-3`: that many Khimera slots per generation, with
the Empty slot on top.

`-ExtraArgs` adds arguments to every pass. It refuses `--hook` (pick a pass instead),
`--with-static-worlds` together with `gerpocalypse` (the hook would drop it), and
`--skip-output` for a pass that must run output.

### The fuzz-meta file

`fuzzer/khimera_damg.yaml` is passed with `-m` by default, as an absolute path, because `fuzz.py`
runs from `Archipelago/`, where a path relative to this repository does not resolve. `-NoMeta`
leaves it out, and `-Meta <path>` points at another file.

It currently holds an empty mapping under the game name and no constraints. The key must stay
even while empty: a file with no mapping at all loads as `None`, and the fuzzer crashes with
`'NoneType' object has no attribute 'get'` before any generation. The game name contains a
colon, so the key is quoted.

### Results

Every run gets a folder, `fuzzer/runs/<timestamp>/`, holding:

- `run.json` -- the parameters, the SHA-256 of the fuzzed apworld, the source fingerprint and time
  of the prepare that built it, and the commits of this repository, of `Archipelago/` and of the
  fuzzer;
- one folder per pass, with `command.txt` (the exact `fuzz.py` command line), fuzz.py's
  `report.json`, its `error/` folder of failing YAMLs and logs, and `result.json` (counts, rate,
  verdict, notes, and the five most frequent error messages).

`fuzz.py` itself writes to `Archipelago/fuzz_output` and wipes that folder at the start of every
run; the pass script moves its content into the archive as soon as the pass ends. Old run folders
are never deleted automatically, and `-Setup` keeps them.

A verdict is one of `ok`, `fail`, `error` (the pass could not start, or `fuzz.py` crashed) or
`stalled` (`fuzz.py` gave up on generations whose workers died; the counts cover only what
finished).

The console shows a `UserWarning` about security issues from `ModuleUpdate.py` at the start of a
run. It is expected on the default interpreter, 3.11.9; see "Fresh clone" in `CLAUDE.md`.

### The canary

    scripts/run_fuzzer.ps1 -Pass canary

`scripts/fuzzer/build_canary_apworld.ps1` writes a ten-location world, `kdamg_canary`, whose pool
is one item short and whose victory needs an item that does not exist, into
`Archipelago/custom_worlds/`. The canary then runs the `rate` and `item_location_count` passes over
it, capped at 50 generations, and expects every one of them to fail. It removes the world again
afterwards, so it is never loaded during a real measurement.

Run it after changing anything in this pipeline, or after a fuzzer update. A canary pass that
comes back `fail` means failures are being hidden.

## The Empty world

`empty-apworld` (<https://github.com/ionium-ap/empty-apworld>) is the 100-free-location world the
index measures the failure rate with. Having it in every generation separates a restrictive start
from a real logic failure.

`scripts/fuzzer/build_empty_apworld.ps1` clones it into `fuzzer/empty-apworld`, repacks it into
`Archipelago/custom_worlds/empty.apworld`, and checks the result loads. The repack exists for the
manifest reason above: upstream's `archipelago.json` omits `version` and `compatible_version`
just like ours does, so the script injects both, taking `container_version` out of
`Archipelago/worlds/Files.py`. The clone keeps its own `.git`, so it can be pulled or re-pinned by
hand. Run the script directly with `-Force` to re-clone and rebuild.

The passes add the Empty slot through the fuzzer's own `with_empty` hook
(`hooks/with_empty.py`), the same route the index uses. It leaves outcomes untouched, so it can
sit next to a checking hook. It writes an Empty YAML to a temporary folder and points
`--with-static-worlds` there; outside the index's container it does not load `empty.apworld`
itself, and relies on the world already being registered, which `custom_worlds/empty.apworld`
provides. It is always loaded first, so if Empty is missing its worker setup fails before any
other hook is registered, and the error reaches the report as a plain failure.

The script also writes `Archipelago/static_worlds/empty.yaml`, for running `fuzz.py` by hand with
`--with-static-worlds static_worlds` instead of the hook.

## Why passes

Each fuzzer hook is written to be run on its own. A hook's `reclassify_outcome` turns every
outcome it is not testing into a success (or an `OptionError`), and `fuzz.py` applies every
loaded hook's reclassification in turn. Loading all six counted hooks in one run gives this:

- `gerpocalypse` turns anything without "no connected region" in its message into a success.
  Fill errors, pool/location mismatches, indirect-condition and capture errors, and timeouts all
  disappear there, and `item_location_count` does the same for anything that is not its own
  mismatch.
- `gerpocalypse` also replaces `--with-static-worlds` with a Kingdom Hearts YAML of its own, so
  the Empty slot is never added while it is loaded.
- `detect_output_placement_changes` wraps only `generate_output`, so under `--skip-output` it
  never fires, and `fill_slot_data` is never exercised either.

Such a run reports 0 failures whatever the world does. The pass table above avoids that: one
checking hook per pass, Empty wherever it can be, and output run where a hook needs it. The
canary is there to notice if the pipeline ever drifts back.

`gerpocalypse` needs the Kingdom Hearts world (`worlds/kh1`, part of Archipelago). Without it,
the hook's worker setup raises inside every generation and its own reclassification would turn
that into a success, so the pass script refuses to start the pass when the world is missing.

## Running fuzz.py by hand

For anything the passes do not cover, run `fuzz.py` from `Archipelago/` with the build venv, in
the prepared state (`scripts/fuzzer_prepare.ps1` first, `scripts/fuzzer_cleanup.ps1` after).
Nothing checks the build's freshness for you here, so prepare again after changing
`khimera_damg/`. Keep to one checking hook per run:

    ..\.py-env\venv\Scripts\python.exe fuzz.py -r 500 -j 16 -g khimera_damg -n 1-5 --hook hooks.with_empty:Hook
